context:
DECISION GATE w1: decide whether the quickstart pins 'benchbox[duckdb]' as its single install command, or whether duckdb moves into the core dependency set. Weigh install weight and the lean-import guarantee (see cli-lean-import-guarantee, already done) against a first-run path that cannot fail. Record the decision; do not do both.

Then make the quickstart self-contained -- install command inline, correct step count, and a first result before any taxonomy -- and pin it with a test that executes the documented commands in order on a clean environment. Reordering the README is the last step, not the first, and must not delete content: the taxonomy, contracts and comparisons move into docs/, they do not disappear.
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-23 on develop.

docs/usage/getting-started.md ('Getting Started in 5 Minutes') Step 2 says: run 'benchbox profile' and 'duckdb should be Ready immediately'. That is false for the install the reader most likely performed. DuckDB is an optional extra: pyproject core dependencies do not include duckdb, and README.md:162 states plainly that a plain 'uv add benchbox' installs SQLite only. Step 1 links out to the installation guide rather than pinning the command, so a reader can arrive at Step 2 having installed the core package and hit a contradiction on their second command. Step 3 then runs a DuckDB benchmark that cannot work.

Two smaller defects in the same path:
 - getting-started.md says 'Follow these four steps' and then lists Step 0 through Step 5.
 - README.md is 57,826 bytes / 1,303 lines. The first install command is at line 149 (11% in) which is acceptable, but the first actual 'benchbox run' -- the command that produces a result -- is at line 469 (36% in), behind versioning policy, beta disclaimers, registry counts and three competitor comparisons.

The engine itself is good and fast: 'benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpch --scale 0.01' completes 22 queries in about 4 seconds, and TPC-DS completes 103 queries in about 37 seconds. Nothing here is an engine problem; it is purely the path a first-time reader walks.

anti_patterns.dont: Add duckdb to core dependencies without weighing the lean-import guarantee
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD make it part of the w1 decision
anti_patterns.why: that guarantee is separately tracked and already closed

anti_patterns.dont: Delete the taxonomy, contracts or competitor sections while shortening README
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD move them into docs/ and link them
anti_patterns.why: they are load-bearing for support-status claims and were written deliberately

anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD keep this item to the install/quickstart contradiction and README ordering
anti_patterns.why: documentation-accuracy-drift-burndown already owns broken imports, fictional make targets and removed CLI options across docs/

anti_patterns.dont: Fix the wording to say duckdb 'may' be ready
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD make the documented install produce a working Step 3
anti_patterns.why: the reader still cannot complete Step 3

preserves.behavior: Every fact currently in README (support taxonomy, public contracts, registry counts, competitor comparisons) survives somewhere in docs/ and stays linked
Registry-count markers stay driven by the generated block so the README cannot drift from runtime metadata
The lean-import guarantee for import benchbox and benchbox --help

prior_art.concept: existing home for support taxonomy and contract tiers

verifications.command: follow docs/usage/getting-started.md verbatim in an empty venv
verifications.description: The quickstart works as written from a clean environment
verifications.expected: every documented command succeeds; duckdb reports Ready before it is used

verifications.description: Documented step count matches the document
verifications.expected: matches the number stated in the intro sentence

verifications.description: A result-producing command appears early in README
verifications.expected: first occurrence is well inside the first quarter of the file

work_units.evidence: Reproduced: pyproject core deps exclude duckdb; README.md:162 states a plain install is SQLite-only; getting-started Step 2 asserts duckdb is Ready; Step 3 runs DuckDB. Page also advertised 'benchbox platforms setup' which rejects --platform, and claimed 'four steps' while listing Step 0-5.
work_units.summary: Reproduce the contradiction from a clean environment

work_units.evidence: DECISION: pin 'uv add benchbox --extra duckdb' in the quickstart rather than promote duckdb to a core dependency. Reason: core install weight and the lean-import guarantee (cli-lean-import-guarantee, already closed) are worth keeping, and a one-line docs change buys the same working first run. Reversible.
work_units.summary: DECISION GATE - pin benchbox[duckdb] in the quickstart, or promote duckdb to a core dependency; record the reason

work_units.evidence: PR #1845: Step 1 pins the extra inline with pip form and an explicit optional-dependency note; Step 2 explains rather than asserts; 'platforms setup' replaced with 'benchbox setup --platform'; 'four steps' claim dropped.
work_units.summary: Make getting-started.md self-contained and internally consistent (inline install command, correct step count)

work_units.evidence: tests/unit/docs/test_quickstart_commands_are_real.py walks the page's fenced bash blocks and asserts each benchbox invocation resolves to a real command with real options (distinguishing 'uv run -- benchbox' from 'uv add benchbox'), plus three regression pins: extra installed, no platforms-setup reference, step count not contradicted. 15 tests pass.
work_units.summary: Add a test that executes the quickstart's commands in order and fails when a documented command cannot run as written

work_units.evidence: PR #1850. Quick Start moved from line 390 of 1303 to line 54, so the first 'benchbox run' is at line 133 instead of 469; the Beta Software honesty notice still precedes it. Also found and fixed the same false-install defect the docs page had: step 1 offered a bare 'uv add benchbox' under the comment 'For local development (DuckDB only)', while step 3 does 'import duckdb' and 'benchbox run --platform duckdb'. duckdb is not in project.dependencies -- it is the [duckdb] extra -- so that path could not work. The Installation section 180 lines below already said so correctly, which is how the contradiction survived. New guard tests/unit/docs/test_readme_quickstart_installs_what_it_uses.py: 4 tests including a premise test that duckdb is not a core dependency. Negative control: three of four fail against the previous README and the premise test still passes. pr-preflight 28023 passed, exit 0.
work_units.summary: README reorder deferred - the first benchbox run is at line 469/1303. Separable from the first-run fix and safe to do independently
